headline: Markets head into the week still digesting a confirmed AI correction
body: Friday's close left the Nasdaq Composite having confirmed a correction, more than 10% below the record it set in early October, after a stretch of trading in which chipmakers and other AI-infrastructure names absorbed most of the selling. The catalyst wasn't disappointing earnings so much as a broader repricing of how long investors are willing to fund heavy AI capital spending before it shows up in returns, and that unease was compounded by the November 3 midterm results, which revived worries about tougher regulatory scrutiny of the large tech and chip platforms. Single-session moves were unusually sharp for the period — the Nasdaq's worst day of the stretch fell somewhere in the mid-single-digit percentage range — and volatility measures stayed elevated rather than settling by week's end, even as trading outside the mega-cap tech cohort was comparatively orderly.

The tone entering the new week reads as unsettled rather than panicked. Nothing in the coverage points to a broad macro deterioration or a credit-market scare; this looks more like a narrow but forceful repricing of a handful of mega-cap and semiconductor names whose valuations had run furthest ahead of near-term fundamentals. Concrete, same-day retail chatter — WallStreetBets or StockTwits trending-ticker color specific to this stretch — was thin in what surfaced, so this read leans on price action, the capex-versus-returns debate, and the post-midterm regulatory overhang rather than on confirmed social-sentiment specifics. That combination argues for a market that is cautious and still arguing with itself about AI valuations, not one that has thrown in the towel.
